claims.text: What the image looks like Schatzki ring → intermittent dysphagia for solids
claims.quote: Schatzki ring → intermittent dysphagia for solids

claims.text: A 2- to 4-mm mucosal stricture causing a ringlike narrowing of the distal esophagus at the squamocolumnar junction; often causes dysphagia
claims.quote: A lower esophageal ring is a 2- to 4-mm mucosal stricture that causes a ringlike narrowing of the distal esophagus at the squamocolumnar junction that often causes dysphagia.

claims.text: Esophageal (Schatzki) rings: smooth, concentric, mucosal folds that narrow the esophagus at the esophagogastric junction
claims.quote: Esophageal rings (also called Schatzki rings) are smooth, concentric, mucosal folds that narrow the esophagus at the esophogastric junction.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Evaluation of dysphagia typically begins with upper endoscopy, which should show a ring large enough to cause symptoms; if the distal esophagus is adequately distended, barium radiographs usually also show the ring
claims.quote: Typically, evaluation of dysphagia begins with upper endoscopy, which should show a ring large enough to cause symptoms. If the distal esophagus is adequately distended, barium radiographs usually also show the ring.

claims.text: Symptoms usually occur only when the esophageal lumen is < 12 mm in diameter and almost never when it is > 20 mm
claims.quote: Symptoms usually occur only when the esophageal lumen is < 12 mm in diameter and almost never when it is > 20 mm (3).

claims.text: Causes Etiology unknown; may be congenital or caused by gastroesophageal reflux or pill-induced esophagitis
claims.quote: The etiology of lower esophageal rings is unknown; they may be congenital or caused by gastroesophageal reflux or pill-induced esophagitis (1).

claims.text: Symptoms Intermittent dysphagia for solids; can begin at any age but usually not until middle adulthood; the swallowing difficulty comes and goes and is especially aggravated by meat and dry bread
claims.quote: These rings cause intermittent dysphagia for solids. Symptoms can begin at any age but usually do not begin until middle adulthood, with a mean age of presentation of 57 years in one study (2). The swallowing difficulty comes and goes and is especially aggravated by meat and dry bread.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Chewing food thoroughly, with sips of water, is usually the only treatment required in wider rings; narrow-lumen rings require dilation by endoscopy or bougienage; surgical resection is rarely required
claims.quote: Instructing the patient to chew food thoroughly, with sips of water, is usually the only treatment required in wider rings, but narrow-lumen rings require dilation by endoscopy or bougienage (dilation with a thin rod of rubber or plastic). Surgical resection is rarely required.
